newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania blames blast on ex-communist forces.
newsitem.headline: Albania blames blast on ex-communist forces.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Alexander Meksi on Wednesday blamed former communist secret policemen for an explosion which injured a top judge and his six-year-old daughter in their apartment during the night.

"I think the authors of the explosion had political motives. It is...those forces of the secret police Sigurimi of the ex-communist regime that aim to destabilise Albanian democracy," Meksi told reporters.

No-one was killed in the attack but judge Prel Martini, 40, his six-year-old daughter Dea and neighbour Kozeta Prendi, 34, were injured, Albanian state radio said. Dea's condition was stable while her parents were in shock.
"A powerful explosion set by unidentified persons destroyed almost completely Prel Martini's apartment," the radio said.

Martini also blamed ex-communists for the attack. "It was ... an effort by the remnants of the (communist regime)...to attack with arms the forces of the police and of justice," he said on radio Tirana.

Late on Tuesday Albania's appeals court upheld prison sentences of up to 20 years for nine senior ex-communist officials. Martini was quoted by the daily Rilindja Demokratike as saying the sentences could be the reason for the explosion.
Police said they did not yet know what kind of device caused the blast. The ministry said a special group had been set up to investigate the case.
Security was stepped up on Wednesday in the capital, with a heavier than usual police presence causing traffic congestion.
Four people were killed and 27 injured last February when a car bomb exploded in central Tirana.
Police later arrested members of what they called a guerrilla organisation comprising former communist secret policemen and charged them with planting the bomb.
